# Best MagSafe car mounts (Oct 2026)

For most iPhone drivers I'd pick the Belkin BoostCharge Qi2 vent mount. Anker is the pick if you want the fastest charging, and ESR or LISEN are the budget options.

| Pick | Best for | Charging | Price |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Belkin BoostCharge Qi2 Vent Mount** | Most people | Qi2, up to 15W | $47.99 |
| **Anker Prime (A2933) MagGo AirCool** | Fastest charging, hot climates | Qi2, up to 25W | $89.99 (one source saw $69.99) |
| **ESR HaloLock CryoBoost** | Value with a cooling fan | Qi2, 15W | $18.99 to $39.99 (sources differ) |
| **LISEN 15W vent/dash mount** | Tight budget | 15W | $15.99 |

## Belkin BoostCharge (best overall)
- It includes a 1m USB-C cable and a 27W car adapter, so nothing else is needed.
- It rotates between portrait and landscape, and takes cases up to 3 mm thick.
- Check your vents first. Belkin's specs call for slats up to 3 mm thick and 20 mm deep. Straight horizontal slats work best, and vertical ones can droop.
- Buy links and details: [RottenWiFi review](https://rottenwifi.com/best-magsafe-car-mounts-in-2026-connect-charge-and-drive/)

## Anker Prime (fastest, best cooling)
- It has thermoelectric cooling plus a fan, which helps navigation and charging at once without throttling. The MountGuys reviewer uses it daily and calls it the easiest recommendation.
- **25W only applies to newer phones.** The iPhone 17 and 16 Pro Max/Plus get up to 25W, the iPhone 16 and 16 Pro get 22W, and iPhone 15 and earlier get about 15W.
- It does not fit Tesla or Mercedes-Benz vehicles, or cars without standard vent blades.
- Sources disagree on the adapter. MountGuys and The Gadgeteer say a 60W adapter is in the box, while RottenWiFi says you need a 45W+ adapter. Confirm on the listing before you buy.
- Links: [MountGuys review](https://www.mountguys.com/best-magsafe-car-mount/) and [The Gadgeteer roundup](https://the-gadgeteer.com/2026/06/16/best-magsafe-car-mounts-iphone-2026/)

## ESR HaloLock CryoBoost (value with a fan)
- It's Qi2-certified at 15W, with a fan and both vent and dash mounting.
- Prices vary a lot. The Gadgeteer lists $18.99, while Dealectric shows $39.99, or $32.80 with code PARTNER18 (valid through 2026-12-31).
- A car adapter isn't confirmed as included, so budget $10 to $15 more.
- [Buy at ESR via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/esr-halolock-15w-wireless-car-charger-cryoboost) (affiliate link, same price to you)

## LISEN (budget)
- The 15W version at $15.99 mounts on the vent or dash. It needs a car port that supplies at least 18W.
- LISEN also makes a 25W fan-cooled version from $39.95 with a 95W adapter included, according to [The Gadgeteer](https://the-gadgeteer.com/2026/06/16/best-magsafe-car-mounts-iphone-2026/). That claim comes from the roundup and I couldn't verify it.

## Tips
- Look for a **Qi2 certification badge**. "MagSafe-compatible" alone can mean slower 7.5W charging.
- Ignore "80 lb suction" claims. They usually describe the dash base, not how well the magnets hold your phone.
- Android phones need a magnetic Qi2 or MagSafe-compatible case to attach.

If you tell me your phone, your car (especially the vent style), and your budget, I can narrow this to one pick.
